claim: Telencephalic area Dp of adult zebrafish is homologous to piriform cortex.
source: We therefore examined effects of E/I assemblies on autoassociative memory in a spiking network model that was constrained by experimental data from telencephalic area Dp of adult zebrafish, which is homologous to mammalian piriform cortex (Mueller et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Mueller et al., 2011

claim: Dp and piriform cortex receive direct input from mitral cells in the olfactory bulb.
source: Dp and piriform cortex receive direct input from mitral cells in the olfactory bulb (OB) and have been proposed to function as autoassociative memory networks (Haberly, 2001; Wilson and Sullivan, 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Haberly, 2001 and Wilson and Sullivan, 2011

claim: Dp and piriform cortex have been proposed to function as autoassociative memory networks.
source: Dp and piriform cortex receive direct input from mitral cells in the olfactory bulb (OB) and have been proposed to function as autoassociative memory networks (Haberly, 2001; Wilson and Sullivan, 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Haberly, 2001 and Wilson and Sullivan, 2011

claim: Manipulations of neuronal activity in piriform cortex affected olfactory memory.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, manipulations of neuronal activity in piriform cortex affected olfactory memory (Meissner-Bernard et al., 2019; Sacco and Sacchetti, 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to Meissner-Bernard et al., 2019 and Sacco and Sacchetti, 2010

claim: Odors evoke temporally structured, spatially distributed activity patterns in Dp and piriform cortex.
source: In both brain areas, odors evoke temporally structured, spatially distributed activity patterns (Blazing and Franks, 2020; Stettler and Axel, 2009; Yaksi et al., 2009) that are dominated by synaptic inputs from recurrent connections (Franks et al., 2011; Rupprecht and Friedrich, 2018) and modified by experience (Chapuis and Wilson, 2011; Frank et al., 2019; Jacobson et al., 2018; Pashkovski et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to experimental studies

claim: Odor-evoked activity patterns in Dp and piriform cortex are dominated by synaptic inputs from recurrent connections.
source: In both brain areas, odors evoke temporally structured, spatially distributed activity patterns (Blazing and Franks, 2020; Stettler and Axel, 2009; Yaksi et al., 2009) that are dominated by synaptic inputs from recurrent connections (Franks et al., 2011; Rupprecht and Friedrich, 2018) and modified by experience (Chapuis and Wilson, 2011; Frank et al., 2019; Jacobson et al., 2018; Pashkovski et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Franks et al., 2011 and Rupprecht and Friedrich, 2018

claim: Odor-evoked activity patterns in Dp and piriform cortex are modified by experience.
source: In both brain areas, odors evoke temporally structured, spatially distributed activity patterns (Blazing and Franks, 2020; Stettler and Axel, 2009; Yaksi et al., 2009) that are dominated by synaptic inputs from recurrent connections (Franks et al., 2011; Rupprecht and Friedrich, 2018) and modified by experience (Chapuis and Wilson, 2011; Frank et al., 2019; Jacobson et al., 2018; Pashkovski et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple experimental studies

claim: Neurons in posterior Dp received large excitatory and inhibitory synaptic inputs during odor responses.
source: Whole-cell voltage clamp recordings revealed that neurons in posterior Dp (pDp) received large E and I synaptic inputs during odor responses.
evidence: Based on experimental measurements using whole-cell voltage clamp recordings

claim: Excitatory and inhibitory inputs in pDp neurons were co-tuned in odor space.
source: These inputs were co-tuned in odor space and correlated on fast timescales, demonstrating that pDp enters a transient state of precise synaptic balance during odor stimulation (Rupprecht and Friedrich, 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Rupprecht and Friedrich, 2018

claim: pDp enters a transient state of precise synaptic balance during odor stimulation.
source: These inputs were co-tuned in odor space and correlated on fast timescales, demonstrating that pDp enters a transient state of precise synaptic balance during odor stimulation (Rupprecht and Friedrich, 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Rupprecht and Friedrich, 2018

claim: Network models of pDp with assemblies but without E/I co-tuning generated persistent attractor dynamics.
source: We found that network models of pDp with assemblies but without E/I co-tuning generated persistent attractor dynamics and exhibited a biologically unrealistic broadening of the firing rate distribution.
evidence: Result from computational simulations described in the manuscript

claim: Network models of pDp with assemblies but without E/I co-tuning exhibited a biologically unrealistic broadening of the firing rate distribution.
source: We found that network models of pDp with assemblies but without E/I co-tuning generated persistent attractor dynamics and exhibited a biologically unrealistic broadening of the firing rate distribution.
evidence: Result from computational simulations described in the manuscript

claim: Introducing E/I assemblies established E/I co-tuning in the network model.
source: Introducing E/I assemblies established E/I co-tuning, stabilized the firing rate distribution, and abolished persistent attractor states.
evidence: Result from computational simulations described in the manuscript

claim: Introducing E/I assemblies stabilized the firing rate distribution in the network model.
source: Introducing E/I assemblies established E/I co-tuning, stabilized the firing rate distribution, and abolished persistent attractor states.
evidence: Result from computational simulations described in the manuscript

claim: Introducing E/I assemblies abolished persistent attractor states in the network model.
source: Introducing E/I assemblies established E/I co-tuning, stabilized the firing rate distribution, and abolished persistent attractor states.
evidence: Result from computational simulations described in the manuscript

claim: In networks with E/I assemblies, responses to learned inputs were locally constrained onto manifolds.
source: In networks with E/I assemblies, population activity was locally constrained onto manifolds that represented learned and related inputs by 'focusing' activity into neuronal subspaces.
evidence: Result from computational simulations described in the manuscript

claim: The covariance structure of manifolds in networks with E/I assemblies supported pattern classification when information was retrieved from selected neuronal subsets.
source: The covariance structure of these manifolds supported pattern classification when information was retrieved from selected neuronal subsets.
evidence: Result from computational simulations described in the manuscript

claim: Networks with E/I assemblies transformed the geometry of neuronal coding space.
source: Networks with E/I assemblies therefore transformed the geometry of neuronal coding space, resulting in continuous representations that reflected both relatedness of inputs and an individual's experience.
evidence: Result from computational simulations described in the manuscript

claim: Networks with E/I assemblies resulted in continuous representations that reflected both relatedness of inputs and an individual's experience.
source: Networks with E/I assemblies therefore transformed the geometry of neuronal coding space, resulting in continuous representations that reflected both relatedness of inputs and an individual's experience.
evidence: Result from computational simulations described in the manuscript

claim: Continuous representations in networks with E/I assemblies enable fast pattern classification.
source: Such continuous representations enable fast pattern classification, can support continual learning, and may provide a basis for higher-order learning and cognitive computations.

claim: Continuous representations in networks with E/I assemblies can support continual learning.
source: Such continuous representations enable fast pattern classification, can support continual learning, and may provide a basis for higher-order learning and cognitive computations.

claim: Continuous representations in networks with E/I assemblies may provide a basis for higher-order learning and cognitive computations.
source: Such continuous representations enable fast pattern classification, can support continual learning, and may provide a basis for higher-order learning and cognitive computations.
evidence: Speculative statement based on computational results

claim: Autoassociative memory establishes internal representations of specific inputs.
source: Autoassociative memory establishes internal representations of specific inputs that may serve as a basis for higher brain functions including classification and prediction.

claim: Representation learning in autoassociative memory networks involves experience-dependent synaptic plasticity.
source: Representation learning in autoassociative memory networks is thought to involve experience-dependent synaptic plasticity and potentially other mechanisms that enhance connectivity among assemblies of excitatory neurons (Hebb, 1949; Ko et al., 2011; Miehl et al., 2023; Ryan et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies

claim: Classical theories proposed that assemblies define discrete attractor states.
source: Classical theories proposed that assemblies define discrete attractor states and map related inputs onto a common stable output pattern.

claim: Brain areas with memory functions such as the hippocampus or neocortex often exhibit irregular firing patterns.
source: However, brain areas with memory functions such as the hippocampus or neocortex often exhibit dynamics that is atypical of attractor networks including irregular firing patterns, transient responses to inputs, and high trial-to-trial variability (Iurilli and Datta, 2017; Renart et al., 2010; Shadlen and Newsome, 1994).
evidence: Supported by citations to experimental studies

claim: Irregular, fluctuation-driven firing reminiscent of cortical activity emerges in recurrent networks when neurons receive strong excitatory and inhibitory synaptic input.
source: Irregular, fluctuation-driven firing reminiscent of cortical activity emerges in recurrent networks when neurons receive strong excitatory (E) and inhibitory (I) synaptic input (Brunel, 2000; Shadlen and Newsome, 1994; van Vreeswijk and Sompolinsky, 1996).
evidence: Supported by citations to theoretical studies

claim: In balanced state networks, enhanced connectivity among assemblies of E neurons is prone to generate runaway activity unless matched I connectivity establishes co-tuning.
source: In such 'balanced state' networks, enhanced connectivity among assemblies of E neurons is prone to generate runaway activity unless matched I connectivity establishes co-tuning of E and I inputs in individual neurons.
evidence: Based on theoretical understanding of balanced networks

claim: Precise synaptic balance stabilizes firing rates because inhomogeneities in excitation across the population or temporal variations in excitation are tracked by correlated inhibition.
source: The resulting state of 'precise' synaptic balance stabilizes firing rates because inhomogeneities in excitation across the population or temporal variations in excitation are tracked by correlated inhibition (Hennequin et al., 2017; Hennequin et al., 2014; Lagzi and Fairhall, 2024; Rost et al., 2018; Vogels et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to theoretical studies

claim: E/I co-tuning has been observed experimentally in cortical brain areas.
source: E/I co-tuning has been observed experimentally in cortical brain areas (Bhatia et al., 2019; Froemke et al., 2007; Okun and Lampl, 2008; Rupprecht and Friedrich, 2018; Wehr and Zador, 2003) and emerged in simulations that included spike-timing-dependent plasticity at I synapses (Lagzi et al., 2021; Litwin-Kumar and Doiron, 2014; Vogels et al., 2011; Zenke et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to experimental studies

claim: E/I co-tuning emerged in simulations that included spike-timing-dependent plasticity at I synapses.
source: E/I co-tuning has been observed experimentally in cortical brain areas (Bhatia et al., 2019; Froemke et al., 2007; Okun and Lampl, 2008; Rupprecht and Friedrich, 2018; Wehr and Zador, 2003) and emerged in simulations that included spike-timing-dependent plasticity at I synapses (Lagzi et al., 2021; Litwin-Kumar and Doiron, 2014; Vogels et al., 2011; Zenke et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to computational studies

claim: E/I co-tuning can be established by including I neurons in assemblies, resulting in 'E/I assemblies'.
source: In simulations, E/I co-tuning can be established by including I neurons in assemblies, resulting in 'E/I assemblies' where I neurons track activity of E neurons (Barron et al., 2017; Eckmann et al., 2024; Lagzi and Fairhall, 2024; Mackwood et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to computational studies

claim: Exploring the structural basis of E/I co-tuning in biological networks is challenging because it requires the dense reconstruction of large neuronal circuits at synaptic resolution.
source: Exploring the structural basis of E/I co-tuning in biological networks is challenging because it requires the dense reconstruction of large neuronal circuits at synaptic resolution (Friedrich and Wanner, 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Friedrich and Wanner, 2021

claim: pDpsim comprised 4000 E neurons and 1000 I neurons.
source: pDpsim comprised 4000 E neurons and 1000 I neurons, consistent with the estimated total number of 4000–10,000 neurons in adult zebrafish pDp (unpublished observations).
evidence: Model specification based on experimental estimates

claim: The estimated total number of neurons in adult zebrafish pDp is 4000–10,000.
source: pDpsim comprised 4000 E neurons and 1000 I neurons, consistent with the estimated total number of 4000–10,000 neurons in adult zebrafish pDp (unpublished observations).

claim: The network received afferent input from 1500 mitral cells in the OB with a mean spontaneous firing rate of 6 Hz.
source: The network received afferent input from 1500 mitral cells in the OB with a mean spontaneous firing rate of 6 Hz (Friedrich and Laurent, 2004; Friedrich and Laurent, 2001; Tabor and Friedrich, 2008).
evidence: Model specification based on experimental data cited

claim: Odors were modeled by increasing the firing rates of 10% of mitral cells to a mean of 15 Hz and decreasing the firing rates of 5% of mitral cells to a mean of 2 Hz.
source: Odors were modeled by increasing the firing rates of 10% of mitral cells to a mean of 15 Hz and decreasing the firing rates of 5% of mitral cells to a mean of 2 Hz (Methods, Figure 1B, Friedrich and Laurent, 2004; Friedrich and Laurent, 2001).
evidence: Model specification based on experimental data cited

claim: During odor stimulation, the mean activity of mitral cells increased only slightly while the variance of firing rates across the mitral cell population increased approximately sevenfold.
source: As a result, the mean activity increased only slightly while the variance of firing rates across the mitral cell population increased approximately sevenfold, consistent with experimental observations (Friedrich and Laurent, 2004; Wanner and Friedrich, 2020).
evidence: Model behavior consistent with experimental observations cited

claim: pDpsim consisted of sparsely connected integrate-and-fire neurons with conductance-based synapses.
source: pDpsim consisted of sparsely connected integrate-and-fire neurons with conductance-based synapses (connection probability ≤5%, Methods).

claim: The mean firing rate in pDpsim was <0.1 Hz in the absence of stimulation and increased to ~1 Hz during odor presentation.
source: The mean firing rate was <0.1 Hz in the absence of stimulation and increased to ~1 Hz during odor presentation (Figure 1C, F; Blumhagen et al., 2011; Rupprecht et al., 2021; Rupprecht and Friedrich, 2018).
evidence: Model results consistent with experimental data cited and shown in figures

claim: Population activity in pDpsim was odor-specific.
source: Population activity was odor-specific and activity patterns evoked by uncorrelated OB inputs remained uncorrelated in pDpsim (Figure 1H; Yaksi et al., 2009).
evidence: Model results consistent with experimental data cited and shown in figures

claim: Activity patterns evoked by uncorrelated OB inputs remained uncorrelated in pDpsim.
source: Population activity was odor-specific and activity patterns evoked by uncorrelated OB inputs remained uncorrelated in pDpsim (Figure 1H; Yaksi et al., 2009).
evidence: Model results consistent with experimental data cited and shown in figures

claim: In pDpsim, inputs from other E neurons contributed >80% of the excitatory synaptic conductance during odor presentation.
source: The synaptic conductance during odor presentation substantially exceeded the resting conductance and inputs from other E neurons (recurrent inputs) contributed >80% of the excitatory synaptic conductance (Figure 1G).

claim: pDpsim entered a balanced state during odor stimulation.
source: Hence, pDpsim entered a balanced state during odor stimulation (Figure 1D, E) with recurrent input dominating over afferent input, as observed in pDp (Rupprecht and Friedrich, 2018).
evidence: Model results shown in figures and consistent with experimental data cited

claim: Shuffling spike times of inhibitory neurons in pDpsim resulted in runaway activity with a probability of 0.79 ± 0.20.
source: Shuffling spike times of inhibitory neurons resulted in runaway activity with a probability of 0.79 ± 0.20, demonstrating that activity was inhibition-stabilized (Sadeh and Clopath, 2020b; Tsodyks et al., 1997).

claim: Activity in pDpsim was inhibition-stabilized.
source: Shuffling spike times of inhibitory neurons resulted in runaway activity with a probability of 0.79 ± 0.20, demonstrating that activity was inhibition-stabilized (Sadeh and Clopath, 2020b; Tsodyks et al., 1997).
evidence: Model results demonstrating inhibition-stabilized activity, with citations to relevant literature

claim: pDpsim reproduced key features of pDp.
source: pDpsim therefore reproduced key features of pDp.
evidence: Summary statement based on model results

claim: An assembly in the model was generated by identifying the 100 E neurons that received the most connections from the mitral cells activated by a given odor.
source: An assembly was generated by identifying the 100 E neurons that received the most connections from the mitral cells activated by a given odor and increasing the probability of connections between these E neurons by a factor of α (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Model specification described in text and shown in figures

claim: In each network, 15 assemblies representing memories of uncorrelated odors were created.
source: In each network, we created 15 assemblies representing memories of uncorrelated odors.

claim: Approximately 30% of E neurons were part of an assembly.
source: As a result, ~30% of E neurons were part of an assembly, with few neurons participating in multiple assemblies.

claim: Odor-evoked activity within assemblies was higher than the population mean and increased with α.
source: Odor-evoked activity within assemblies was higher than the population mean and increased with α (Figure 2B).

claim: When α reached a critical value of ~6, networks became unstable and generated runaway activity.
source: When α reached a critical value of ~6, networks became unstable and generated runaway activity (Figure 2B).

claim: In Scaled I networks, correlations between E and I synaptic conductances in individual neurons remained near zero.
source: In Scaled I networks, correlations remained near zero, indicating that E assemblies by themselves did not enhance E/I co-tuning (Figure 2H).

claim: E assemblies by themselves did not enhance E/I co-tuning.
source: In Scaled I networks, correlations remained near zero, indicating that E assemblies by themselves did not enhance E/I co-tuning (Figure 2H).
evidence: Inference from model results shown in figures

claim: Scaled I networks with structured E but random I connectivity cannot account for the stability, synaptic balance, and E/I co-tuning observed experimentally.
source: Scaled I networks with structured E but random I connectivity can therefore not account for the stability, synaptic balance, and E/I co-tuning observed experimentally (Rupprecht and Friedrich, 2018).
evidence: Inference from model results compared to experimental data cited

claim: In Tuned networks, correlations between E and I conductances in individual neurons were significantly higher than in rand or Scaled I networks.
source: In Tuned networks, correlations between E and I conductances in individual neurons were significantly higher than in rand or Scaled I networks (Figure 2H).

claim: Tuned networks exhibited significant co-tuning along the balanced axis.
source: Hence, Tuned networks exhibited significant co-tuning along the balanced axis, as observed in pDp (Rupprecht and Friedrich, 2018).
evidence: Model results consistent with experimental data cited

claim: In Tuned networks, activity within assemblies was substantially lower and more irregular than in Scaled I networks.
source: In Tuned networks, activity within assemblies was higher than the mean activity but substantially lower and more irregular than in Scaled I networks (Figure 2E, G; Figure 2—figure supplement 2).

claim: In Tuned networks, mean firing rates evoked by novel odors were indistinguishable from those evoked by learned odors.
source: Unlike in Scaled I networks, mean firing rates evoked by novel odors were indistinguishable from those evoked by learned odors and from mean firing rates in rand networks (Figure 2F, Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).

claim: E/I co-tuning prevented excessive amplification of activity in assemblies without affecting global network activity.
source: Hence, E/I co-tuning prevented excessive amplification of activity in assemblies without affecting global network activity, consistent with experimental observations in Dp and piriform cortex (Chapuis and Wilson, 2011; Frank et al., 2019).
evidence: Inference from model results consistent with experimental data cited

claim: Rand networks showed transient and variable responses to input patterns.
source: Hence, rand networks showed transient and variable responses to input patterns, consistent with the typical behavior of generic balanced state networks (Shadlen and Newsome, 1994; van Vreeswijk and Sompolinsky, 1996).
evidence: Model results consistent with theoretical understanding cited

claim: Scaled I networks responded to learned odors with persistent firing of assembly neurons and high pattern correlations across trials and time, implying attractor dynamics.
source: Scaled I networks responded to learned odors with persistent firing of assembly neurons and high pattern correlations across trials and time, implying attractor dynamics (Hopfield, 1982; Khona and Fiete, 2022), whereas Tuned networks exhibited transient responses and modest pattern correlations similar to rand networks (Figure 2E).
evidence: Model results shown in figures and interpreted based on theoretical understanding cited

claim: Tuned networks exhibited transient responses and modest pattern correlations similar to rand networks.
source: Scaled I networks responded to learned odors with persistent firing of assembly neurons and high pattern correlations across trials and time, implying attractor dynamics (Hopfield, 1982; Khona and Fiete, 2022), whereas Tuned networks exhibited transient responses and modest pattern correlations similar to rand networks (Figure 2E).

claim: Tuned networks did not exhibit stable attractor states.
source: Hence, Tuned networks did not exhibit stable attractor states, presumably because precise synaptic balance prevented strong recurrent amplification within E/I assemblies.

claim: Precise synaptic balance prevented strong recurrent amplification within E/I assemblies.
source: Hence, Tuned networks did not exhibit stable attractor states, presumably because precise synaptic balance prevented strong recurrent amplification within E/I assemblies.

claim: Stimulating subsets of E neurons in an assembly during baseline activity recruited the entire assembly in all structured pDpsim networks.
source: Stimulating subsets of E neurons in an assembly during baseline activity recruited the entire assembly in all structured pDpsim networks (Scaled and Tuned) without a significant increase in the overall population activity (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).

claim: In rand networks, output correlations increased linearly with input correlations but did not exceed them.
source: In rand networks, output correlations increased linearly with input correlations but did not exceed them (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), consistent with the absence of pattern completion in generic random networks (Babadi and Sompolinsky, 2014; Marr, 1969; Schaffer et al., 2018; Wiechert et al., 2010).
evidence: Model results shown in figures and consistent with theoretical understanding cited

claim: Scaled I networks showed typical signatures of pattern completion.
source: Scaled I networks, in contrast, showed typical signatures of pattern completion: output correlations increased abruptly as a morphed odor approached a learned odor and eventually exceeded the corresponding input correlations (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).

claim: In Tuned networks, output correlations were higher than in rand networks but remained lower than input correlations.
source: In Tuned networks, output correlations were higher than in rand networks but remained lower than input correlations and did not increase steeply near the learned odor (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).

claim: Networks with E/I assemblies did not show signatures of pattern completion in response to naturalistic stimuli.
source: Hence, networks with E/I assemblies did not show signatures of pattern completion in response to naturalistic stimuli, consistent with the absence of strong recurrent amplification within assemblies.

claim: In rand networks, the linear increase in activity of pseudo-assembly neurons can be attributed entirely to an increase in afferent input.
source: This linear increase in activity can be attributed entirely to an increase in afferent input (Figure 3D) because the net recurrent input remained constant due to E/I balance (Figure 3E).

claim: In Scaled networks, assembly firing rates increased massively as the learned odor was approached, reflecting a large increase in recurrent excitation.
source: In Scaled networks, assembly firing rates increased massively as the learned odor was approached (Figure 3C), reflecting a large increase in recurrent excitation (Figure 3D–F, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).

claim: In Tuned networks, assembly firing rates increased only modestly due to a slightly larger increase in E than I currents near the learned odor.
source: In Tuned networks, in contrast, assembly firing rates increased only modestly due to a slightly larger increase in E than I currents near the learned odor (Figure 3D–F, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).

claim: The modest amplification by assemblies of Tuned networks involves an 'imperfect' synaptic balance.
source: Hence, the modest amplification by assemblies of Tuned networks involves an 'imperfect' synaptic balance.

claim: Correlations between OB activity patterns representing pure odors and mixtures decreased approximately linearly as a function of distance in the odor subspace.
source: Correlations between OB activity patterns representing pure odors and mixtures decreased approximately linearly as a function of distance in the subspace (Figure 4B).

claim: The distribution of OB activity patterns in PC space closely reflected the square geometry of the odor subspace.
source: As expected, the distribution of OB activity patterns in PC space closely reflected the square geometry of the subspace (Figure 4C).

claim: In Scaled I networks, odor inputs were discretely distributed between three locations in state space representing the two learned odors and residual odors.
source: In Scaled I networks, odor inputs were discretely distributed between three locations in state space representing the two learned odors and residual odors, consistent with the expected discrete attractor states (Figure 4D, E).

claim: Tuned networks generated continuous representations of the odor subspace.
source: Tuned networks, in contrast, generated continuous representations of the odor subspace (Figure 4D).

claim: The geometry of representations in Tuned networks was distorted in the vicinity of learned odors.
source: The geometry of these representations was distorted in the vicinity of learned odors, which were more distant from most mixtures than novel odors.

claim: E/I assemblies introduced local curvature into the coding space that partially separated learned from novel odors without disrupting the continuity of the subspace representation.
source: Hence, E/I assemblies introduced local curvature into the coding space that partially separated learned from novel odors without disrupting the continuity of the subspace representation.

claim: Dimensionality was highest in rand networks and very low in Scaled I networks.
source: As expected, dimensionality was highest in rand networks and very low in Scaled I networks, reflecting the discrete attractor states (Figure 4F).

claim: In Tuned networks, dimensionality was high compared to Scaled I networks but lower than in rand networks.
source: In Tuned networks, dimensionality was high compared to Scaled I networks but lower than in rand networks (Figure 4F).

claim: When restraining the analysis to activity evoked by novel odors and related mixtures, dimensionality was similar between rand and Tuned networks.
source: Furthermore, when restraining the analysis to activity evoked by novel odors and related mixtures, dimensionality was similar between rand and Tuned networks (Figure 4F).

claim: E/I assemblies locally constrain neuronal activity onto lower-dimensional subspaces (manifolds).
source: These observations support the hypothesis that E/I assemblies locally constrain neuronal activity onto lower-dimensional subspaces (manifolds), consistent with recent findings showing effects of specific circuit motifs on the dimensionality of neural activity (Dahmen et al., 2023; Recanatesi et al., 2019).
evidence: Inference from model results consistent with recent findings cited

claim: In Tuned networks, the variance of activity patterns related to novel odors decreased only slightly as a function of PC rank.
source: In Tuned networks, this variance decreased only slightly as a function of PC rank for activity patterns related to novel odors, indicating that patterns varied similarly in all directions.

claim: For patterns related to learned odors in Tuned networks, the variance was substantially higher in the direction of the first few PCs.
source: For patterns related to learned odors, in contrast, the variance was substantially higher in the direction of the first few PCs, implying variation along preferred dimensions.

claim: Angles between edges connecting activity patterns were narrowly distributed around 1 rad in rand networks but smaller in the vicinity of learned patterns in Tuned networks.
source: Angles were narrowly distributed around 1 rad in rand networks but smaller in the vicinity of learned patterns in Tuned networks (Figure 4H).

claim: E neurons participating in E/I assemblies had large loadings on the first two PCs.
source: E neurons participating in E/I assemblies had large loadings on the first two PCs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F, G) and responded to learned odors with increased firing rates as compared to the mean rates in Tuned E+I and rand networks.

claim: Firing rates of non-assembly neurons were slightly lower than the corresponding mean rates in rand networks.
source: Firing rates of the remaining neurons, in contrast, were slightly lower than the corresponding mean rates in rand networks.

claim: The variance of activity projected onto the first few PCs was higher in Tuned E+I than in rand networks.
source: Consistent with these observations, the variance of activity projected onto the first few PCs was higher in Tuned E+I than in rand networks (Figure 4G) while the variance along higher-order PCs was lower (Figure 4G, inset).

claim: The variance of activity along higher-order PCs was lower in Tuned E+I than in rand networks.
source: Consistent with these observations, the variance of activity projected onto the first few PCs was higher in Tuned E+I than in rand networks (Figure 4G) while the variance along higher-order PCs was lower (Figure 4G, inset).

claim: Local activity manifolds are delineated both by amplification of activity along preferred directions and by suppression of activity along other dimensions.
source: These observations indicate that local activity manifolds are delineated both by amplification of activity along preferred directions and by suppression of activity along other dimensions.

claim: Equalizing biophysical parameters of E and I neurons had little impact on network behavior.
source: Equalizing biophysical parameters of E and I neurons had little impact on network behavior (Figure 4—figure supplement 2; Methods), indicating that observed effects do not depend on specific biophysical differences between E and I neurons.

claim: The modest amplification of activity within E/I assemblies contributes to the geometry of neural manifolds in pDpsim.
source: These results indicate that the modest amplification of activity within assemblies contributes to the geometry of odor representations in pDpsim.

claim: dM was asymmetrically increased in Tuned E+I networks as compared to rand networks.
source: dM was asymmetrically increased in Tuned E+I networks as compared to rand networks. Large increases were observed for distances between patterns related to learned odors and reference classes representing novel odors (Figure 5A, B).

claim: The geometric transformation of odor representations by E/I assemblies particularly enhanced the discriminability of patterns representing learned odors.
source: The geometric transformation of odor representations by E/I assemblies therefore particularly enhanced the discriminability of patterns representing learned odors.

claim: In Tuned E+I networks, the classification probability of mixtures similar to a pure odor was significantly higher when the pure odor was learned.
source: Furthermore, in Tuned E+I networks, the classification probability of mixtures similar to a pure odor was significantly higher when the pure odor was learned (Figure 5C).

claim: E/I assemblies facilitated the classification of inputs related to learned patterns.
source: Hence, E/I assemblies facilitated the classification of inputs related to learned patterns.

claim: When neuronal subsets were randomly drawn from the entire population, dM was generally lower than when drawn from assemblies.
source: When neuronal subsets were randomly drawn not from assemblies but from the entire population, dM was generally lower (Figure 5B).

claim: Assembly neurons convey higher-than-average information about learned odors.
source: These results indicate that assembly neurons convey higher-than-average information about learned odors.

claim: pDpsim did not function as a categorical classifier but nonetheless supported the classification of learned odors, particularly when the readout focused on assembly neurons.
source: Together, these observations imply that pDpsim did not function as a categorical classifier but nonetheless supported the classification of learned odors, particularly when the readout focused on assembly neurons.

claim: Lowest prediction errors for odor concentration were observed for concentration estimates of learned odors in Tuned networks.
source: Lowest errors were observed for concentration estimates of learned odors in Tuned networks.

claim: Highest accuracy in estimating odor concentrations was found for learned odors in Tuned networks.
source: We further trained support vector machines to estimate the concentrations of pure odors in the subspace mixtures and again found highest accuracy for learned odors in Tuned networks (Figure 5F).

claim: Networks with E/I assemblies enable the quantitative analysis of selected stimulus components in the presence of distractors.
source: These results show that networks with E/I assemblies enable the quantitative analysis of selected stimulus components in the presence of distractors, presumably due to the geometric properties of the underlying neural manifold.

claim: In Tuned networks, introducing additional overlapping assemblies selectively increased the discriminability of the corresponding odor representations in PC space.
source: In Tuned networks, introducing additional overlapping assemblies selectively increased the discriminability of the corresponding odor representations in PC space (Figure 6B, C), as observed for uncorrelated assemblies (Figure 4D), but population firing rates remained almost unchanged (Figure 6B, C).

claim: In Scaled I networks, creating two additional memories resulted in a convergence of the corresponding representations in PC space and in a substantial increase in firing rates.
source: In Scaled I networks, in contrast, creating two additional memories resulted in a convergence of the corresponding representations in PC space and in a substantial increase in firing rates, particularly in response to the learned and related odors (Figure 6C).

claim: Precise balance in E/I assemblies protects networks against instabilities during continual learning, even when memories overlap.
source: These observations are consistent with the assumption that precise balance in E/I assemblies protects networks against instabilities during continual learning, even when memories overlap.

claim: Global inhibition was insufficient to stabilize population activity in simulated networks with assemblies.
source: However, as seen in Scaled I networks, global inhibition is insufficient to maintain a stable, biologically plausible firing rate distribution.

claim: pDpsim recapitulated characteristic properties of a biological memory network with precise synaptic balance.
source: Hence, pDpsim recapitulated characteristic properties of a biological memory network with precise synaptic balance.
evidence: Summary statement based on model results

claim: Simulated networks with global inhibition showed attractor dynamics and pattern completion.
source: Simulated networks with global inhibition showed attractor dynamics and pattern completion, consistent with classical attractor memory.

claim: The distribution of firing rates broadened in networks with global inhibition as connection density within assemblies increased.
source: However, the distribution of firing rates broadened as connection density within assemblies increased, resulting in unrealistically high (low) rates inside (outside) assemblies and, consequently, in a loss of synaptic balance.

claim: In networks with E/I assemblies, firing rates remained within a realistic range and the balanced state was maintained.
source: In networks with E/I assemblies, in contrast, firing rates remained within a realistic range and the balanced state was maintained.

claim: Tuned networks showed no discrete attractor states but transformed the geometry of the coding space by confining activity to continuous manifolds near representations of learned inputs.
source: Such Tuned networks showed no discrete attractor states but transformed the geometry of the coding space by confining activity to continuous manifolds near representations of learned inputs.

claim: E/I co-tuning decreases the probability of multistable attractor states as compared to balanced networks with global inhibition or lateral inhibition between assemblies.
source: This observation is consistent with the hypothesis that E/I co-tuning decreases the probability of multistable attractor states as compared to balanced networks with global inhibition or lateral inhibition between assemblies (Boerlin et al., 2013; Hennequin et al., 2018; Wu and Zenke, 2021).
evidence: Inference from model results consistent with theoretical understanding cited

claim: Transformations in Tuned networks became more discrete map-like when amplification within assemblies was increased and precision of synaptic balance was reduced.
source: We found that transformations became more discrete map-like when amplification within assemblies was increased and precision of synaptic balance was reduced.

claim: Decreasing amplification in assemblies of Scaled networks changed transformations toward the intermediate behavior.
source: Likewise, decreasing amplification in assemblies of Scaled networks changed transformations toward the intermediate behavior, albeit with broader firing rate distributions than in Tuned networks (Figure 4—figure supplement 3B).

claim: Precise synaptic balance may generally favor intermediate over discrete transformations because this regime tends to linearize the relationship between the mean input and output firing rates of neuronal populations.
source: Nonetheless, our results suggest that precise synaptic balance may generally favor intermediate over discrete transformations because this regime tends to linearize the relationship between the mean input and output firing rates of neuronal populations (Baker et al., 2020; Denève and Machens, 2016).
evidence: Inference from model results consistent with theoretical understanding cited

claim: Balanced networks with E/I assemblies are generally consistent with experimental observations in piriform cortex and Dp.
source: Balanced networks with E/I assemblies, in contrast, are generally consistent with these experimental observations.
evidence: Inference from model results compared to experimental observations

claim: Pattern completion and its modulation by learning has been observed in piriform cortex of rodents.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, pattern completion and its modulation by learning has been observed in piriform cortex of rodents (Barnes et al., 2008; Chapuis and Wilson, 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to experimental studies

claim: Odor-evoked firing patterns in piriform cortex and Dp are typically irregular, variable, transient and less reproducible than in the OB even after learning.
source: However, odor-evoked firing patterns in piriform cortex and Dp are typically irregular, variable, transient and less reproducible than in the OB even after learning (Jacobson et al., 2018; Pashkovski et al., 2020; Schoonover et al., 2021; Yaksi et al., 2009), indicating that activity does not converge onto stable attractor states.
evidence: Supported by citations to experimental studies

claim: The hypothesis that memory networks contain E/I assemblies and operate in a state of precise synaptic balance can be derived from the basic assumptions that synaptic plasticity establishes assemblies and that firing rate distributions remain stable as network structure is modified by experience.
source: The hypothesis that memory networks contain E/I assemblies and operate in a state of precise synaptic balance can be derived from the basic assumptions that (1) synaptic plasticity establishes assemblies and (2) that firing rate distributions remain stable as network structure is modified by experience (Barron et al., 2017; Hennequin et al., 2017).
evidence: Inference based on theoretical understanding cited
